e: ElastiCache for Redis in front of the database serves hot metadata from memory in sub-millisecond time, and Redis supports snapshots and replication, which Memcached doesn't. Scaling the database alone won't help, and Aurora replicas or DynamoDB global tables don't provide sub-millisecond caching with minimal change.

Add the development OU's ARN to the AMIs' launch permissions so every account in that OU can launch them, and update the KMS key policy to allow the OU's accounts to use the key that decrypts the encrypted snapshots. Without KMS access the shared AMIs can't be launched.

80 PB in 4 weeks can't move over 1 to 2 Gbps links, so use multiple Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices at each office (about 1 PB per office). Direct Connect for each office is slow and costly, Snowmobile is for a single site at exabyte scale, and Storage Gateway is bandwidth-limited.

An EFS file system resource policy that denies elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite to the applications' IAM roles enforces read-only access through IAM, so the apps can't modify or delete the dataset. Mount options and POSIX permissions can be changed on the client side, and EFS identity policies aren't set on the file system.

Create an IAM role in the company's account that trusts the vendor's account (or IAM role), with only the needed permissions; the vendor's tool assumes it to get temporary credentials, with no long-term credentials (an external ID can be added). IAM users with passwords or keys are less secure.

Cost allocation tags label resources by department owner for accountability, and AWS Budgets usage budgets with an alert threshold at 60% notify the CFO when spending reaches that level. Anomaly Detection and Trusted Advisor don't create budget threshold alerts.

Instances in private subnets behind an internal ALB are reachable only from inside the VPC (the office over the Site-to-Site VPN), with the ALB security group allowing only the office CIDR, and NAT gateways in public subnets provide outbound internet access for security patches. Public ALBs would expose the application.

Amazon QLDB is a managed ledger database that provides an immutable, cryptographically verifiable journal of all data changes, ideal for accounting records with minimal operational support. Redshift, Neptune, and Timestream don't offer that verifiable ledger.

AWS Step Functions orchestrates the DataBrew data preparation jobs, running them in parallel and in a specific order, with built-in error handling, retries, and state management, so the company doesn't build that logic itself. Lambda chains, Athena scheduling, or Data Pipeline lack that orchestration.

An SQS FIFO queue provides exactly-once processing and message deduplication, so each due payment is processed once, and Lambda polls the queue to process payments. Standard queues can deliver duplicates, and S3 events or DynamoDB streams don't guarantee no duplicates.

AWS Application Discovery Service collects server configuration, usage, and performance data from on-premises servers, and Migration Hub (with its home Region set) centralizes that data to plan the migration. SCT, DMS, Trusted Advisor, and Systems Manager don't do application discovery.

AWS Control Tower in the management account sets up a governed multi-account environment with CloudTrail logging across all accounts (including new ones through Account Factory), and Security Hub flags noncompliance with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard, with low overhead. Control Tower can't be deployed in a member account.

A Glue crawler catalogs the Parquet logs and Athena runs SQL directly on the data in S3, paying only per query, which is the most cost-effective for occasional analysis of 10 TB. Aurora, Redshift, or EMR clusters carry continuous cost.

AWS Control Tower proactive controls (based on CloudFormation hooks) check resources before deployment and block CloudFormation stacks that would create noncompliant resources, such as EC2 instances with public IPs or IAM inline policies with elevated access. Detective controls only report afterward, and SCPs can't inspect those resource properties.

An Application Load Balancer in public subnets distributes traffic across instances, and EC2 Auto Scaling across multiple AZs in private subnets provides high availability and scalability without rewriting the application. A bigger instance remains a single point of failure, and a NAT gateway doesn't handle web requests.

Lambda environment variables can be encrypted with a KMS key and encryption helpers so values are encrypted and not shown in plaintext in the console. Certificates, CloudHSM-based SSL, or moving to EC2 don't encrypt Lambda environment variables.

A Cognito user pool handles user sign-up and authentication for millions of users, and API Gateway REST APIs can use a Cognito authorizer to verify tokens, all fully managed. Identity pools issue AWS credentials rather than authenticating users, and Lambda or IAM user authentication requires more effort.

An EventBridge rule on the KMS key deletion event can start a Systems Manager Automation runbook that cancels the deletion (preventing accidental loss) and publish an SNS message to notify administrators, with no custom code. A CloudTrail alarm only notifies, and Config rules or custom Lambda logic add overhead.

Reports take under 10 minutes and are requested rarely and unpredictably, so Lambda (triggered by EventBridge) starts immediately, runs for the short time, and charges only for execution, which is the cheapest and fastest. Always-on EC2 instances cost more, and ECS adds startup delay.

A tightly coupled HPC environment benefits from an Elastic Fabric Adapter on EC2 instances for low-latency, high-throughput inter-node networking, and FSx for Lustre (scratch storage for temporary high-performance data) for fast shared storage. Global Accelerator, CloudFront, and Elastic Beanstalk don't optimize HPC.

Amazon Rekognition provides pretrained content moderation that detects unwanted content in images with no model training, invoked from a Lambda function by the application when photos are uploaded. SageMaker Autopilot needs training, Comprehend is for text, and Rekognition Video is for videos.
AWS lets you register multiple MFA devices for the root user (up to eight), so if one is lost another can be used to sign in. Backup administrator accounts don't recover root-only capabilities.

An SNS topic with HTTP/S subscriptions lets each partner subscribe their endpoint and receive the user IDs when published, so adding hundreds of partners is just adding subscriptions, scalable with the least effort. The other options need custom code for each partner.

Amazon Comprehend is a pretrained NLP service (entity extraction) that needs no ML expertise, invoked from Lambda via an S3 event and storing the extracted names in DynamoDB cost-effectively. Forecast is for time series, Polly is text-to-speech, and SageMaker requires ML knowledge.

With VPC peering between the Lambda function's VPC and the VPC hosting the EFS mount targets in the secondary account (and an access point and file system policy), the function can mount the cross-account file system, which scales with the file system at minimal cost. Copying the data or invoking cross-account functions adds cost and complexity, and layers are size-limited.
